content.value_statement: Angular modules often need shared updates without tight coupling. This skill guides BlueprintEventBus events, subscriptions, lifecycle cleanup, and workflow coordination.
actual_capabilities: Defines a BlueprintEvent shape with type, blueprintId, timestamp, actor, data, and metadata fields.
Shows where to publish task and member events after successful business operations.
Demonstrates subscriptions for single event types, multiple event types, and all events.
Shows blueprintId filtering and takeUntilDestroyed cleanup for Angular components.
Includes examples for audit logging, notifications, activity feeds, workflows, and tests.
limitations: It is documentation and example code, not a packaged Angular library.
It assumes an Angular and RxJS application structure.
Examples use placeholder services such as TaskRepository and NotificationRepository.
It does not define authorization, payload redaction, or retention policies.

use_cases.title: Plan Cross-Module Events
use_cases.description: Design event names, payloads, and boundaries for modules that need shared Blueprint updates.

use_cases.title: Update Feature UI From Events
use_cases.description: Subscribe to task or member events and refresh scoped views without direct service coupling.

use_cases.title: Test Event-Driven Workflows
use_cases.description: Verify event publishing, blueprint filtering, and subscriber behavior for task workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Event
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one feature event.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add BlueprintEventBus support for task creation. Define the event name, payload fields, publish point, and subscriber behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Filter Events by Blueprint
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate UI update for scoped views.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update my Blueprint task list to listen for task changes. Include blueprintId filtering and lifecycle cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Notifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Design event-driven notifications for task assignment and member addition. Include event payloads, subscribers, and failure boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Review Event Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this BlueprintEventBus plan for coupling, event naming, payload size, cleanup, tests, and security risks.

output_examples.input: I need task updates to refresh a Blueprint task list.
output: Recommended events are task.created, task.updated, and task.deleted.
Publish each event only after the repository operation succeeds.
Filter subscribers by blueprintId before updating the visible task list.
Use lifecycle cleanup so old components stop receiving events.

output_examples.input: I want notifications when a task is assigned.
output: Publish a task.assigned event with the task, assignee, actor, and blueprintId.
Subscribe in the notification service and create a user notification.
Keep notification failures separate from the original task update.

output_examples.input: I need to test Blueprint event filtering.
output: Create events for two Blueprint identifiers.
Subscribe with a filter for the target Blueprint identifier.
Assert that only the matching event updates the subscriber state.

best_practices: Publish events after successful state changes, not before them.
Filter by blueprintId when a view or workflow is scoped to one Blueprint.
Use takeUntilDestroyed or equivalent cleanup for every component subscription.
anti_patterns: Using the event bus for request-response flows that should use services.
Broadcasting large or sensitive payloads without redaction rules.
Subscribing to all events when a feature only needs one event type.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps Angular modules communicate through BlueprintEventBus events with typed payloads and scoped subscriptions.

faq.question: Does it include executable scripts?
faq.answer: No. It contains Markdown guidance and TypeScript examples for application code.

faq.question: When should I use BlueprintEventBus?
faq.answer: Use it for cross-module updates, audit trails, notifications, activity feeds, and workflow orchestration.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for parent-child component communication, direct service calls, data fetching, and request-response behavior.

faq.question: How does it handle subscription cleanup?
faq.answer: The examples use takeUntilDestroyed so Angular subscriptions end with the owning component or service lifecycle.

faq.question: Does it define security policy?
faq.answer: No. Teams must add authorization, payload redaction, and retention rules for their own event data.
